instructions: Ask only unanswered questions after the four-question kickoff in START_HERE.md. The kickoff must capture system name, authoritative timezone, work pattern, and exact brief/order cadence. Group no more than four related questions at a time; provision stock briefs, order lifecycle, recipes, and private Git recovery before optional modules. Capture the exact job title and actual duties during kickoff. Ask HOME/ROAD questions only when the role involves recurring driving/travel/overnights; otherwise bypass that branch.

questions.prompt: What should this personal-ops system be called?
Which IANA timezone is authoritative even while you travel?
Does your operational day use a non-midnight boundary because of night work?
How often and at which exact local times should briefs arrive in the authoritative timezone?
Do AM/PM labels match your sleep schedule, or should a slot have a custom name?
How often and at which exact local times should order evidence be checked or summarized?
Should order changes be immediate, digest-only, or immediate only for exceptions?
What is the user's exact job title and what do they actually do?
What is the shift, normal workweek, and recurring work-travel or overnight pattern?
Do you travel for work, and what departures or returns repeat?
For this travel role, what should HOME and ROAD mean operationally?
questions.applies_when: Job title or actual duties involve recurring driving, trucking, delivery routes, field travel, rotating worksites, transport crew, or nights away from home.

questions.prompt: Which household members affect shared purchases, calendars, or task ownership?
Which vehicles or equipment need their own task and document branches?
Which current courses, certifications, or study tracks need exact folders?
Which recurring responsibilities are easy to forget?
What deterministic schedule, departure, arrival, location, or user statement enters and exits each mode?
questions.applies_when: HOME/ROAD routing is enabled for this user.

questions.prompt: Which vacation, early-return, pause, or temporary overrides are needed, and when do they expire?
questions.applies_when: HOME/ROAD routing is enabled for this user.

questions.prompt: Which tasks, appointments, weather, routes, and notifications appear in each mode?
questions.applies_when: HOME/ROAD routing is enabled for this user.

questions.prompt: Which household members need separate mode rules, state, and schedules even when evidence is shared?
questions.applies_when: HOME/ROAD routing is enabled for this user.

questions.prompt: What must the first manual sample brief contain before scheduling is approved?
Which direct or forwarded email accounts contain order, shipment, delivery, cancellation, replacement, return, and refund evidence?
Which order exceptions should notify immediately instead of waiting for the next digest?
Where are the user's recipe documents, PDFs, images, links, or notes currently stored?
Which cuisines, meal types, dietary tags, equipment, or household categories should recipes support?
Which recipe fields must be searchable and filterable: title, ingredient, tag, source, prep time, nutrition, or others?
Should the default recipe view use collapsible headings, cards, or another native readable surface?
How should duplicate or variant recipes preserve provenance without duplicating the canonical body?
How short should the normal brief be?
Which priorities or tiers should tasks use?
Do some items remain visible until explicitly completed?
What must never be repeated after acknowledgement or confirmation?
How should a brief report an unavailable dependency?
What tone, terminology, or forbidden filler should the brief use?
Where should mutable tasks and controls live?
Does an existing Sheet, database, or app already contain authoritative state?
Should completed and removed rows be retained for history?
Which fields are mandatory before a task can be stored?
Which data must never enter prompts, repositories, or shared files?
How long should logs, receipts, and archived records be retained?
Which email account supplies actionable messages, shipments, and receipts?
Which calendar is authoritative for appointments and reminders?
Which Drive or cloud storage should hold evidence and documents?
Which existing private Git repository should store durable policy, or may setup create one?
Which existing task apps or automations must be inspected before creating duplicates?
Is spending analysis email-detected only, or is an account-level source connected?
Should receipts update a tool, vehicle, warranty, or asset inventory?
Should route or severe-weather evidence be used, and under which gate?
After the initial private-repository approval, may every lasting policy/schema/feature change commit and push automatically without asking again?
Should verified changes stop at a branch/PR, or may any bounded merge policy be enabled?
If automatic Git synchronization fails, should the operational change pause or remain locally staged with an Action Required notice?
Which few top-level domains should exist?
Which issued licenses, resumes, and employment records belong under Personal?
Should education file by institution, exact course/certification, then material type?
Which recipe sources should feed the stock searchable, collapsible recipe library and ingredient/tag index?
May contents be read to name and categorize untitled or ambiguous files?
Should versions be preserved, archived, or deduplicated after confirmation?
Should non-movable shared sources be copied into owned organized folders?
Which scheduled tasks already exist, including paused duplicates?
Does the account have an active-task limit that favors multi-time RRULE dispatch?
What should happen if a required connector is unavailable?
Which condition watches should stay silent when nothing changed?
Which scheduled-task mutations require snapshot-and-rollback?
Should the same policy support manual runs from any conversation?
Does any requested workflow depend on a phone, NAS, home server, or LAN-only service?
What explicit bridge or sync mechanism is authorized for private-device access?
What is the narrowest permission each integration needs?
Where will credentials live so they are never pasted into chat or committed?
Which deletes, archives, sends, or overwrites require confirmation?
How often should policy noise, stale state, and duplicate tasks be reviewed?
How will you judge whether the system saves time and catches the right things?
Who may approve lasting policy, schema, schedule, or integration changes?
Who should be able to recover the system if the primary chat thread is gone?
